name: Spiderman Push-Up
description: The Spiderman push-up adds a knee-to-elbow hip flexion movement to each rep of a standard push-up, simultaneously training the chest, triceps, and hip flexors while demanding greater core stability and rotational control. The lateral leg movement also improves hip mobility and increases the cardiovascular demand.

execution.starting_position: Begin in a standard high plank position with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width and body in a straight line.
execution.setup_instructions: No equipment needed. Find a space long enough for a full plank position.
steps: Step 1: Begin in a high plank, bracing the core.
Step 2: As you lower your chest toward the floor, simultaneously bring one knee out to the side and toward the same-side elbow.
Step 3: Touch or bring the knee as close to the elbow as possible at the bottom of the push-up.
Step 4: Press back up and return the leg to the starting position.
Step 5: Alternate legs each rep or complete all reps on one side before switching.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale as you lower down and bring the knee out. Exhale as you press up and return the leg.
common_mistakes: Letting the hip drop on the side of the moving leg
Raising the hip rather than keeping the torso level
Rushing the movement without achieving the knee-to-elbow contact
safety_considerations: Establish solid standard push-up form before adding the leg movement
Move the leg laterally, not forward under the body, to protect the lower back
If hip mobility limits the range, work up to it progressively
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full push-up range combined with the knee moving as far toward the elbow as mobility allows. The goal is simultaneous floor contact of the chest and knee-to-elbow approximation.
coaching_cues: Touch knee to elbow at the bottom
Keep the hips level — don't let them swing
One smooth movement: down and knee out, up and leg back
